name: placement-model
stage: offline (placement-data-v1 only; no new data generation)

data.validation: the last 45 train games (2896405-2896449) choose the epoch; the test split is read once by the gate and never used for fitting or selection
data.known_before_training: 4,000 setup_settlement decisions, 64,000 candidate rows (16 per decision: served top-12 by the served bot's own placement value + 4 uniformly random other legal vertices), 8 playouts each by the game's true lineup; the served placement (served_rank 0) is the in-sample playout-best candidate in 11.8% of decisions (chance 6.25%)

rows.x: encoder-v2 features of the afterstate from the chooser's view (1,324)
rows.extra: the opponents' public style posterior at the decision (3 opponents x 4 styles, seat-relative order), setup_index one-hot (8), served_rank/16; appended to the tile transformer's global token
rows.label: wins/playouts (soft)

model.arch: tile-token transformer as arch_bakeoff.make_net('tiles') (arch-bakeoff-v1 PASS, +.0138 AUC), with the extra inputs concatenated into the global-token projection
model.augment: one of the 12 hex symmetries per row per batch (encoder-v2 permutation before tokenizing)
model.loss: soft BCE to the playout rate + 1.0 x within-decision listwise cross-entropy (softmax over the decision's candidates vs playout rates normalized to sum 1; decisions with all-zero rates contribute BCE only)

baselines.random: a uniformly random candidate (expected value of the mean candidate rate)

gate.primary: on the 50 test games (400 decisions): the model's top-ranked candidate's playout rate minus the served candidate's playout rate; game-clustered bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0 (1,000 resamples, seed 29)
gate.reported: pick minus served by setup_index (first vs second placement) and by seat; mean regret vs the in-sample best candidate (descriptive only: 8-playout selection noise biases it); top-1 agreement with the in-sample best; mean within-decision Spearman between model scores and rates; row log loss and AUC vs the playout rate; the same for the served and random baselines
gate.next: PASS: planner_placement_model (fast: at each setup settlement the served top-K vertices are scored by this model instead of 24 playouts; everything else served) gets a separately predeclared, powered e2e screen on the three tables. FAIL: recorded; no retuning of the bar.

limitations: 8 playouts per candidate make per-row labels noisy (rate SD about .17 at p=.3); the listwise term targets within-decision order, which is what placement choice uses. The data's opponents are the four known styles, so a pass says nothing about unseen opponents. The posterior input is the public one the bot would have at play time.
note: Predeclared 2026-11-08 before any training (Jerry 2026-11-07: 'Yes and allow'; follows placement-infer-screen-v1 FAIL (+.103/+.025/+.031) and arch-bakeoff-v1). Weights stay local; only metadata is committed. Ultra MPS.
